messages:
Sara K.: heads up — noticed a latency spike on the mv-routing canary this morning. P95 jumped from ~85ms to ~220ms after the fallback flood. :eyes:
Tae Kim: ugh, when did it start? any single sample or sustained?
Sara K.: started around 09:12 UTC, sustained for ~8m then partial recovery when traffic dropped. attaching quick flame snapshot in a sec.
Devon P.: perf-bot posted CI alerts earlier: `bench/batching/continuous` regressed on 2 variants. logged as perf-3242.
perf-bot: [perf-3242] benchmark failed: continuous-batcher P95 (baseline 82ms -> 205ms) — artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/3242/*
Noah L.: my initial guess: compat set fragmentation + repeated fallback causing small micro-batches + KV cache churn. those tiny batches kill kernel efficiency.
Sara K.: agree. flame shows much more kernel launch time/overhead and lower occupancy. KV miss rate up ~3x.
Tae Kim: can you paste the flame/sampled stack? also the routing config used for the canary?
Devon P.: paste of relevant bits:
```
routing_policy: multi_variant
compat_sets:
  - [v1-small, v2-quant]
  - [v3-large]
slo: p95 < 100ms
token_budget_per_queue: 128
queue_policy: strict_fifo
fallback: allow_fanout
```
Devon P.: profiler snapshot (trimmed):
```
- continuous_batcher: 48%
- kernel_launch: 22%
- kv_cache_miss_handler: 15%
- scheduling_overhead: 9%
- other: 6%
```
Tae Kim: strict_fifo + allow_fanout + small token budget likely makes the scheduler create many tiny batches when a compatibility mismatch triggers fallback. kernel_launch being 22% is huge.
Noah L.: two quick levers: raise token_budget_per_queue to 256 to let batches coalesce, or change queue_policy to permissive_merge which will merge cross-compatible requests more aggressively. also consider sticky-variant routing to avoid oscillation.
Sara K.: I'd prefer a small-step change: bump token_budget to 192 and change fallback to sequential instead of fanout for the canary. run for 30m and compare KV miss/occupancy.
Devon P.: I'll run a canary patch with these two changes and point the failing traffic at it. running bench now: `./bench/run_continuous --variants multi --duration 30m --token-budget 192 --fallback sequential`
perf-bot: starting benchmark job #3242b (canary-token192-fallback-seq) — ETA 30m
Tae Kim: also add a quick kernel-affinity hint to prefer fused-attention kernels for v2-quant. should reduce kernel_launch. small patch: add `kernel_hint: fused_attention` to v2-quant compat entry.
Noah L.: good call. even a hint can avoid the expensive generic path.
Sara K.: ok team — Devon, run with the hint as well if it's low-risk. I'll watch KV stats and look at batch size distribution.
Devon P.: running now with token=192 + fallback=sequential + kernel_hint. command: `./bench/run_continuous --variants multi --duration 30m --token-budget 192 --fallback sequential --kernel-hint fused_attention`
Devon P.: initial halfway update: average batch size up from 2.1 -> 4.8, KV miss rate down 2.9x, kernel_launch pct down to 12%. latency trending back toward baseline. :thumbsup:
Sara K.: amazing, compile full artifacts when done. we'll keep the canary until end of day if stable, then roll to other pools.
Tae Kim: follow-up action: add a defensible runtime heuristic — when fallback floods happen, temporarily increase token_budget and delay fanout for X seconds. file: runtime/heuristics/fallback_smoothing.md created?
Noah L.: agreed — also add observability: expose compat-set churn metric + per-variant kernel path ratio so we can alert sooner.
Sara K.: logging task and owners:
- Devon: finish canary + upload artifacts to s3 (owner: Devon P.)
- Tae: draft heuristic doc + proposal PR (owner: Tae Kim)
- Noah: add compat churn metric to console dashboard (owner: Noah L.)
- Sara: coordinate rollout and postmortem note if needed (owner: Sara K.)
Devon P.: artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/3242b/ — latency P95 now 88ms, KV miss = baseline*1.1. I'll open the patch to apply token_budget=192 + fallback=sequential + kernel_hint to canary routing.
Sara K.: great. we'll re-evaluate tomorrow AM and consider automating the ephemeral budget bump in the runtime. thanks all.
